Class restated from this row's own instance/ctor/dtor columns; no new measurement beyond the section/containment check.	002465F0	none - built on the caller's stack	SIGNATURE RESOLVED	PROVEN	L2	0x18 from the span the constructor writes and hands over: 0024660A stores the id at [rsp+0x20] and 00246620 movdqu xmmword ptr [rsp+0x28], xmm0 clears [rsp+0x28]..[rsp+0x38], so the record runs +0x00..+0x18. +0x04 IS NOT A FIELD AND IS NOT ZEROED: the id store covers +0x00..+0x04 and the movdqu starts at +0x08, so those four bytes are whatever the stack held. A reimplementation that zero-initialises the whole struct is not reproducing this, and a handler that reads +0x04 is reading uninitialised memory - it is left as a gap deliberately. ARGUMENT POSITION PROVEN before anything was declared: 002465F0 is the INITIALISER, not the contract's Widget_Create. Its rcx is the already-allocated widget (memset target at 00246626, and the object whose +0x00 and +0x40 it writes), rdx is the SIZE (movsxd r8, edx at 00246612 feeding that memset), r8 is the handler (null-checked to the default 005C5230 by 00246635 cmove), r9 is this message pointer, and a fifth stack argument at [rsp+0x80] supplies the pooled bit 14 at 002466DC-002466F2. ORDERING: the handler runs BEFORE the +0xB4 write - 00246748 call rax, then 0024675C mov dword ptr [rdi+0xB4], 1 - so a handler answering the construction message sees +0xB4 at its pre-construction value, not 1 CTOR RECORDED 2026-09-11 FROM EVIDENCE THE STORE ALREADY HELD. A charter section 27 sweep of my own lane measured the lifetime columns across the 44 game types: 16 had a constructor recorded and ONE had a destructor. Checking why, the initialiser was frequently cited in the type's OWN field evidence and simply never lifted into the ctor column - the gap was in the recording, not the research. Eleven types carried initialisation-flavoured citations with no ctor; each candidate was resolved to its containing function and judged individually, and five were REJECTED (see the rejection note on those types). 002465F0, read directly this session. The message is not allocated: the constructor builds it on its OWN STACK at [rsp+0x20], writing the id at +0x00 (0024660A) and the two payload qwords at +0x08/+0x10 under a single null check, then passes that address to the proc at 00246740. So the 'constructor' is the frame that lays it out, which is why this row has no allocation site and should not acquire one. NO DESTRUCTOR, AND THE ANSWER WAS ALREADY IN THIS ROW'S OWN INSTANCE STRING. Section 27 asks how the type is destroyed; where a type has no storage of its own the answer is that it is never destroyed separately, and the instance column had been stating that relationship all along without anyone drawing the lifetime conclusion from it. Callers build one on the stack and pass its address; the constructor's own is at [rsp+0x20], verified this session by reading 002465F0. Stack storage is released by the frame, so there is no teardown to record and none to implement. Recorded 2026-09-11. A reconstruction must give this type no teardown path: freeing or clearing it independently would touch memory owned by the caller.	16-UI/Widget-Object-Model/CONTRACT-widget-object.md
